answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Inducted quality control analyst registration with analysts institute confirmation changes that arithmetic: a registration the institute keeps after batch audits, so the river for each fake is paid in the real world. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the beacon of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head. The prism is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
